news.headline: House Democrats Back Impeachment Resolution Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
news.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeen Jeffries publicly declared a "hard yes" to impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The resolution is expected to be introduced this week, with Democrats supporting it and some Republicans possibly defecting after recent midterm losses. The move reflects heightened partisan tensions and debates over the secretary's conduct and national security policies. The outcome could set a precedent for impeachment proceedings against a sitting cabinet official.

news.headline: Jim Jordan elected House Republican minority leader
news.summary: House Republicans voted in a closed‑door ballot to choose their next minority leader. Rep. Jim Jordan defeated Rep. Steve Scalise in the vote. The leadership change comes after the party's significant losses in the recent midterm elections. Jordan will lead the GOP conference in the 120th Congress.

news.headline: US lawmakers summon Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese spy ties
news.summary: U.S. intelligence officials warned that a woman close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. Republican committee chairs have sent a letter requesting Huang appear before Congress to brief them on the matter. The issue raises concerns about potential espionage and national security risks tied to a leading tech company. The White House later canceled a tech advisory panel that would have included Huang.

news.headline: Republican Senators Debate Delaying Leadership Vote After Midterm Losses
news.summary: Following the GOP's loss of both chambers in the recent midterm elections, several Republican senators are urging a postponement of the party's leadership elections. Senate Majority Leader John Thune is seeking reelection as the GOP's Senate leader despite the pushback. The dispute centers on whether a rushed vote would be appropriate as the party transitions to minority status. The outcome will affect the GOP's strategy and organization heading into the new Congress.

news.headline: California voters reject Proposition 40 billionaire wealth tax
news.summary: California voters voted down Proposition 40, a ballot measure that would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on billionaire fortunes to fund healthcare. The measure faced strong opposition from wealthy donors, business groups, and some political factions, while supporters included progressive lawmakers and economists. The defeat marks a rare midterm setback for wealth‑tax proposals in a state known for liberal policies. The outcome may influence future wealth‑tax efforts in other states.

news.headline: House Oversight Committee releases report on federal handling of Epstein case
news.summary: The Republican-led House Oversight Committee issued a 137-page report detailing alleged failures by federal prosecutors, investigators and financial institutions that allowed Jeffrey Epstein to continue his sexual abuse after 2005. The report clears former President Donald Trump of wrongdoing but calls for further investigation of key witnesses and DOJ practices. The Justice Department responded that the case remains open and some recommendations have already been addressed. The findings highlight ongoing debate over accountability and reform of federal investigations.

news.headline: Prominent Democrats refuse to back Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader
news.summary: Senators Bernie Sanders, Elissa Slotkin and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez announced they will not support Chuck Schumer's bid to become Senate majority leader when Democrats regain control in January. The refusals were echoed by Senator Richard Blumenthal and other lawmakers who called for new leadership and a concrete plan. The dissent highlights internal divisions within the Democratic caucus ahead of the upcoming Congress. The outcome could influence the selection of the party's Senate leader and its legislative agenda.

news.headline: U.S. CPI rises 0.4% in October, slightly above expectations
news.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the consumer price index increased 0.4% month‑over‑month in October, outpacing most forecasts. The rise was driven by higher shelter, food and energy costs, while gasoline prices fell. The data came after a government shutdown delayed some year‑over‑year figures. The reading is closely watched by the Federal Reserve as it assesses monetary policy.

news.headline: Trump offers UFC CEO Dana White White House press secretary position
news.summary: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that he has offered the White House press secretary job to UFC chief Dana White. The post noted that White could bring several UFC fighters as assistants. The offer follows the recent departure of former press secretary Katie Zacharia. The announcement has drawn attention due to White's background in mixed‑martial‑arts promotion.

news.headline: Supreme Court Allows Trump Administration to Resume Border Wall Construction in Big Bend, Texas
news.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court issued an order lifting a lower‑court injunction, permitting the Trump administration to continue building sections of its border wall in the Big Bend National Park area of Texas. The decision overrides environmental challenges and allows the administration to proceed with barriers, roads and surveillance infrastructure while related lawsuits remain pending. The ruling is seen as a significant win for the administration’s immigration‑security agenda.
